candidates.title: $\tau^\tau$-Bench: An Environment for End-To-End, Realistic Agent Construction
candidates.citationVelocity: Published 4 days ago (submitted 2026-09-04); Semantic Scholar: 0 citations
communitySignals: No Papers with Code repo found
No confirmed public code/dataset release link found in the fetched sections
credibilityEvidence: Section 3: seven independently-configurable task levers (evidence surface, client simulator, API fidelity, starting codebase, model menu/budget, live-experiment call, response-phrasing rule) with Appendix A tabulating every setting
Section 4 Table 2 (referenced): 53 release tasks across 4 domains, strongest configuration (Claude Opus 5 + Claude Code) at 23.9% vs expert-authored reference ceiling at 82.2%
Section 6: failure-mode analysis tracing the gap to specification recovery, client interrogation, budget management, and design-space exploration
Appendix G/H: real construction-kit filesystem example and trajectory-log excerpts for a specific release task (010, retail_plus) with step-by-step spec recovery and deployment
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Main results, failure-mode analysis, task-construction statistics tables, and worked trajectory examples all covered; each task configuration is built only once so build-to-build variance is not characterized (disclosed as Limitation 2)
reproducibilityEvidence: Extensive task-statistics tables (Appendix A) and a full sample construction kit / README (Appendix G) are published in the paper
No confirmed public dataset or code download link found in the fetched sections; authors are a commercial company (Sierra) on this exact product line
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Rigorous 53-task, 4-domain methodology with an expert-authored ceiling and itemized failure-mode analysis supports the article's claim strength
candidates.primaryLimitation: Each task configuration is built only once (no build-to-build variance measured); client/user simulator is a single LLM with fixed requirements, simplifying real engagements with multiple conflicting stakeholders
candidates.presentationReason: Seven-lever task formulation, scoring formula, and limitations are all explicitly stated with a comparison table against 6 related benchmarks
candidates.reason: Strongest capability/limits candidate: first benchmark to make 'building a complete deployable agent' itself the scored task rather than testing an already-built agent, with a rigorous 53-task methodology, an expert reference ceiling, and an itemized failure-mode breakdown directly actionable for teams using coding agents to build agents.

candidates.title: Bilevel Coordinated Reflection: A Game-Theoretic Approach to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
candidates.citationVelocity: Published 6 days ago (submitted 2026-09-02); Semantic Scholar: 0 citations
candidates.institution: UCL Centre for Artificial Intelligence + University of Liverpool + Huawei
communitySignals: Code publicly released on GitHub (github.com/YihangChen9/Bilevel-Coordinated-Reflection) for Resource Contest + Overcooked scenarios; 0 stars as of this run
No Papers with Code entry found
credibilityEvidence: Section 3.1: formal proof (Lemma 1, Theorem 1, Corollary 1) that the followers' subgame is an approximate potential game with slack bounded by decomposition coupling

Section 3.3: information-theoretic impossibility theorem that a transcript-only gate cannot uniformly improve over text-indistinguishable environments, with a grounded comparator that converges geometrically

Section 4: three environments (Resource Contest, Overcooked, SWE-bench) with ablations isolating decomposition/memory/grounding effects; Overcooked grounded-SRMA beats self-gating by 14.3-30.0% across 3 layouts; SWE-bench Kimi K2.5 complete system 72.2% vs free-form ungated 58.4%, controlled DeepSeek comparison 71.4% vs 68.2%
Section 4: statistical-resolution experiment showing adaptive confidence gating matches fixed-K=5 reliability (7.1% vs 6.8% false-accept rate) at 82 vs 225 verifier calls
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Theoretical framework, three-environment experiments, ablations, and a controlled cross-backbone (Kimi K2.5, DeepSeek) comparison are all present; the headline 72.2% is compared against an external public leaderboard (70.8%), not a matched-budget controlled run, disclosed by the authors themselves in the Limitations section
reproducibilityEvidence: GitHub repo public for Resource Contest and Overcooked scenarios, confirmed via direct fetch of the repo README
Authors state the SWE-bench scenario code will be released separately 'in about two weeks' — not yet available
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Theory and three-environment experiments corroborate each other with clean ablations; the one weaker comparison (external leaderboard) is self-disclosed in the paper's own Limitations section, not discovered externally
candidates.primaryLimitation: The headline 72.2% SWE-bench result is compared against an external public leaderboard, not a matched-budget controlled run (controlled DeepSeek comparison shows a smaller gap: 71.4% vs 68.2%); theoretical guarantees' preconditions (bounded coupling, finite action sets, calibrated verifier) may not hold in open-ended tasks
candidates.presentationReason: Theorems, proofs, and experimental sections are cleanly separated with an explicit, self-authored Limitations section distinguishing controlled from leaderboard comparisons
candidates.reason: Strongest method/theory candidate: first to connect coordination quality and reflection convergence through a provable game-theoretic + stochastic-approximation framework (not just an empirical recipe), with an impossibility theorem directly explaining why text-only self-reflection gates plateau, validated across three environments including SWE-bench with released code for two of three scenarios.

candidates.title: Where Reliability Lives: Experimental Localisation of Behavioural Properties in an Agent System
candidates.citationVelocity: Published 6 days ago (submitted 2026-09-02); Semantic Scholar: 0 citations
candidates.institution: Not stated in the paper (authors: Timothy Marsden, Matthew Collecutt, James Marsden; no affiliation found)
communitySignals: No Papers with Code repo found
credibilityEvidence: Section 3-4: preregistered interventions on institutional epistemic mechanisms (evidence provenance, belief availability) with the central registered prediction refuted twice, in opposite directions, honestly reported in Section 7.2

Section 5: four cognition-side interventions (ablate native mind machinery, kill-and-reset, substitute entire cognition with a frozen frontier-LLM panel, corrupt beliefs with false testimony) while holding institutional enforcement fixed

Section 6-7: five pre-declared reliability properties (singular accepted reality, typed refusal of invalid attempts, duty persistence, no duplicate work, zero false completions) held across all tested trajectories, including 2,581 substituted-panel claims with zero false completions; Section 7.3 explicitly distinguishes 'load-tested' from merely 'held' properties
Section 8: an unusually extensive threats-to-validity section (one designed world, n=3 cognition-substitution cells, harness not yet public, explicit 'what we do not claim' list)
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Validated only in two fixed scenarios within one designed world; cognition-substitution comparison is n=3 cells with one comparator model; authors explicitly state they make no estimate about a population of institutions
reproducibilityEvidence: Section 10: SHA-256 manifest of sealed artifacts and verification receipts published, with results regenerating byte-identically from archived raw trajectories under frozen scorers
Full experiment harness for independent re-execution is deliberately deferred as future work — not yet available
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The method is extremely rigorous and honest (including disclosing two refuted preregistered predictions), but the evidence scope is narrow (one world, small comparator set) and the authors themselves repeatedly stress the results do not generalize beyond this setting
candidates.primaryLimitation: All results are tested in one designed simulated world across only two fixed scenarios; the cognition-substitution comparator is a single model at n=3 cells; the full re-execution harness is not yet public
candidates.presentationReason: Extremely explicit about claim boundaries — a dedicated 'what this paper does not claim' subsection and a tautology-objection rebuttal preempt likely misreadings
candidates.reason: Selected as the third angle (architecture/safety) to complement today's other two papers: turns 'where does reliability come from' into an intervenable, falsifiable experimental question rather than an architecture-diagram assumption, and is unusually honest about refuted predictions and narrow scope — a natural complement to Bilevel Coordinated Reflection's point about grounded vs. text-only judgment. Weighed against 2609.04198 (Clean Engineering, Unstable Measurement) which was initially considered for this slot but discovered to already be published on 2026-09-06 (hard-dedup exclusion, not a credibility rejection).
